newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iranian foreign minister to visit Saudi - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iranian foreign minister to visit Saudi - paper.

text.p: Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati plans to visit Saudi Arabia next week, the first trip to the kingdom by a senior Iranian official for more than three years, a Saudi-owned newspaper said on Thursday.
It quoted Gulf diplomatic sources as saying Velayati would carry messages from the Iranian leadership on how to improve relations and restore trust between two of the world's biggest oil producers.

Iranian media reports had recently said Velayati would visit Saudi Arabia on a tour to invite Islamic nations to a summit of the Jeddah-based Organisation of the Islamic Conference due to be held in Tehran in December.
Saudi Arabia and other Gulf Arab states have accused their non-Arab neighbour of interfering in their internal affairs -- a charge Iran denies -- and voiced concern over its arms buildup.

Saudi officials have refused to confirm U.S. media reports that Iran was linked to the June bombing of a U.S. housing complex in the kingdom which killed 19 U.S. servicemen. Iran, which has criticised the U.S. and Western military presence in the region, has denied any involvement.

Ties between Iran and Saudi Arabia are usually strained during the annual Moslem pilgrimage to holy sites in the kingdom, with Iran insisting on holding political rallies in defiance of a Saudi ban. The pilgrimage is next month.
